_about: The build-out's bible: what each connector zone is, its mood, the levels of what lives there, and ideas for its creatures and items. Writers work from these (tools/atlas/briefs.py); nothing here is read by the game.
world: The realm is Misthollow. Its heart is Garathorm, a walled city (Garathorm Inner City) whose Temple is where every journey starts. Roads run out from its gates across plains, forests and hills to New Thalos and old Thalos in the east, Port Halyon on the Sea of Storms, the Dwarven Kingdom under the mountains, Haon-Dor's dark wood, and lands still uncharted (sealed until built). The tone is classic fantasy with a weathered, lived-in feel: old roads, older ruins, honest folk, and things in the dark.

408.name: Trade Road
408.theme: The web of roads that binds Garathorm to the realm, and the country they cross. Next to the city lie Garathorm's outer streets (Danozi Avenue, Pasocaoa Boulevard, Stonewalk Way, Esh Road, Shokogya Street and the Trade Road itself): a busy merchant town outside the walls, named for the traders from the east who built it, with homes, a brewery and a leatherworker. The King's Road runs past the Great Field and Welmar's Castle into the Radiant Forest, a wood of pale gold leaves where the light seems to linger (the Path of Light runs through it), and on into the Old Forest and the gloomier Trail of Shadows toward the elven lands of Elvandar and the King's Forest. North and east the Birch Woods and the Meadow Thrithing, a long grass meadow, lead down to the shore of the Long Lake and a rangers' camp. The open Plains and the Never Ending Plains roll away past a ruined road and the Gate of Kashmir. The Caravan Road and the Old Temple Road run through the farm village of Hommlet, its Church of Helver and its craftsmen; the Dusty Road runs through a small village near Salem's Lot; a muddy path leads to the Dead Marshes; the Black Woods are dark and close; vineyards lie by the Great Field.
408.mood: Busy and safe by the city (carts, travellers, the watch), pastoral on the plains and meadows, golden and calm in the Radiant Forest, wild and uneasy in the Old Forest, the Trail of Shadows and the Black Woods.
408.creatures: Low levels (3-10) by the city and on the plains: stray dogs, pickpockets, field hares, wild boar. Middling (10-20) in the forests and meadows: wolves, highwaymen, giant spiders, bears. Higher (20-30) in the Black Woods, on the Trail of Shadows and far out on the Never Ending Plains: dire wolves, outlaw captains, wraiths, a wandering ogre. Nothing hostile in the outer streets.
408.items: Things travellers and bandits carry: a highwayman's short sword, a waymark charm, a ranger's cloak, wolf pelts to sell, trail rations.

50.name: Great Eastern Desert
50.theme: Despite the name, this stretch is the desert's hidden water: a river that runs out of the eastern sands into a gorge, rapids, a river bend and a lake, then under the mountain as the Dark River through caves, tunnels and an underground lake. Deep inside are fungus patches and a Fungus Temple of the myconids, a cave-in, a wind-swept ledge and a mysterious lair. It joins the Trade Road, Garathorm, New Thalos, the Sea of Storms, the Plains, Drow City, the Dragon's Domain and the sunken ruins of Atal'narath.
50.mood: Sun-bleached rock and fast brown water outside; cool, dripping, echoing dark inside; strange and fungal at its heart.
50.creatures: River and cave life (5-15): river crabs, cave bats, giant frogs, blind cave fish shoals, kobold scavengers. Deeper (15-28): myconid sentries (the myconids are already here), cave trolls, rock lurkers.
50.items: Glowing fungus caps, a river-smoothed stone charm, a spelunker's lantern, a myconid spore-pouch.

60.name: Plains
60.theme: The country west of Garathorm: open plains, the deep dark forest of Miden'nir with its narrow trails, junctions and dead ends, a swift river running to a delta, a beach head and a pier, and the island of Minos with its seven Trials. It already has many of our creatures (goblins, rabbits, squirrels, foxes, wolves, wyverns).
60.mood: Open and windy on the plains, dense and shadowed under the trees, salt and reeds at the delta, solemn at the Trials of Minos.
60.creatures: Top up only: river otters, herons and marsh snakes at the delta and river (3-10), a goblin scout band in the deep forest (8-14).
60.items: A heron feather, a goblin's notched dagger, an otter-skin pouch.

40.name: Mountain Range
40.theme: Moria's surface and the foothills around it: mountain trails, cliffs and chasms, an illuminated ravine, western foothills and a copse of trees, and a warren of tunnels and caves underneath (the Golden Cave, the Light Cave, the Large Cave, a maze, a shortcut, a secret tunnel and chamber, the Hill Giant Cave). It already has kobolds, orcs, snakes, hobgoblins, a mountain lion and a hill giant.
40.mood: Thin cold air and long views above; close, dripping, echoing dark below.
40.creatures: Top up only: mountain goats and hawks on the trails (3-8), a cave bear and rock spiders in the caves (12-20).
40.items: A miner's pick, goat-horn trinket, a hawk-feather fletching kit.

435.name: MiNar I
435.theme: The Great Forest of MiNar, a vast old-growth wilderness, with the Grasslands around it and the country just outside its eaves; Wilderness Way crosses it, and an obscure path or two. In its depths: Farrot's Nest, the Warrior's Grove, a big tree, the lounge of two retired adventurers (Mortis and Sojat) and the Rahn Mercenary Camp where swords are hired. It joins the Plains, the Tunnel of Sticks and Mira Retrum II.
435.mood: Enormous, quiet and green under the canopy, every stretch subtly different (mossy, fern-choked, sun-dappled, root-tangled, misty); the grasslands are wide, windy and bright.
435.creatures: Forest life (5-15): stags and does, boar, timber wolves, owlbears, giant forest spiders, woodland sprites; on the grasslands: wild horses, prairie wolves, hawks; at the mercenary camp: Rahn mercenaries (not hostile).
435.items: Antler-handled knife, mercenary's leather jerkin, owlbear claw, a sprig of MiNar heartwood.

61.name: Haon-Dor (Dark)
61.theme: The dark heart of Haon-Dor: a spider queen's den, a great web, a tree, an underground hallway and a cultist temple. Its rooms are already written; it needs only a few items for the spiders and cultists it holds (Isha the dark elf, the elder druid, the queen spider).
61.mood: Sticky webs, rot and whispering darkness.
61.items: Spider silk, a venom sac, a cultist's black candle, the queen spider's fang.

120.name: Sea of Storms
120.theme: The great eastern sea and the coast around Port Halyon. The open Sea of Storms and its ocean currents (cross-currents, a sharp turn, around an island), the shoreline, a canal and the docks; Port Halyon's waterfront (River Avenue, Wharf Avenue, a warehouse and its basement, the Capitol's records rooms and the dock master's office); a stretch of the Great Eastern Desert with a small oasis, a nomad camp and camels; and, above the port, a darker quarter: Vice Hill, the Tarry Tunnels (a waiting room, an outlay, a screening room, a torture chamber), the Trail of Terror and the Temple of Terror (blindingly lit halls, a hall of wax, the high priest's office), the Building of Fear (creepy halls, a wailing tower, a trophy room), and the ruins of Dim Carcosa with its black building, the green stairs of faith and rooms of death. It already has the people of Port Halyon (citizens, gladiators, gateguards, dervishes).
120.mood: Salt wind, gulls and rope on the waterfront; heaving grey water at sea; heat and glare in the desert; dread, wax and incense in the terror quarter; ancient silence in Carcosa.
120.creatures: Top up: gulls, crabs and sea snakes on the shore and docks (3-10), sharks and a sea serpent at sea (15-30), dune scorpions and desert raiders in the desert (10-20), cultists of terror and wax effigies in the terror quarter (20-30), shades in Carcosa (25-34).
120.items: Sailor's knife, sharkskin boots, a cultist's terror mask, a Carcosan coin, a nomad's water flask.

441.name: King's Forest
441.theme: A small hilly wood off the King's Road: a rocky path, a barrow mound, a stone ledge, a cave, an old well and a badger's burrow, and someone's hiding place.
441.mood: Quiet, old and a little eerie around the barrow.
441.creatures: Badgers and foxes (6-10), a barrow wight (14-16), a poacher in hiding (10-12).
441.items: A barrow-blade, a poacher's snare, a tarnished grave-ring.

448.name: Mira Retrum I
448.theme: A wide, calm inland sea south of the Plains, bordered by white sand beaches and the Southern Ocean beyond, with Leper Island's beach offshore and the mouth of Quickstream. Mostly open water: a boat or a raft is needed.
448.mood: Bright, shallow, gentle; sunlit swells, drifting weed and sea birds; lonely far out.
448.creatures: Easy sea life (1-8): gulls, jellyfish, sand crabs on the beaches, a playful seal, a giant clam.
448.items: A pearl, a conch shell horn, a crab-shell buckler, dried seaweed.

66.name: Northern Wilderness
66.theme: The cold north beyond the Trade Road: open tundra and taiga, mountains, a narrow crack in a glacier, icy slopes, an ice bridge, a cave and a cabin. It joins the Goblin Warrens, the Great Northern Forest, the Winterwood, the Eastern Highlands, Mount Ravenmist and the sealed Cave Elf Kingdom. It already has bandits, deer, wolves, a bear and a travelling merchant.
66.mood: Bitter wind, endless white and grey, the creak of ice.
66.creatures: Top up: snow hares and arctic foxes (3-8), a frost wolf pack and a yeti (12-20).
66.items: Fur-lined boots, a yeti's pelt, a bone ice-pick.

451.name: Mira Retrum II
451.theme: The colder southern and south-eastern reaches of Mira Retrum, among drifting icebergs and narrow straits, around Cape Voogk to a quiet bay beyond an ice wall and an ocean cave; it touches the shore of the Great Forest of MiNar and the sealed Submerged Temple. A boat or a raft is needed.
451.mood: Grey, cold and vast; ice groaning, mist on the water, seals barking from floes.
451.creatures: Seals and penguins on the floes (6-9), ice crabs, a killer whale and frost sea-serpent further out (12-16).
451.items: Walrus-ivory charm, sealskin cloak, a frost-pearl.

472.name: Mount Ravenmist
472.theme: A tall, mist-wrapped mountain north of the realm: long mountain paths, the Crescent Cliffs, a tall tower wall (the Outcast Fortress is near), a dark cave, the mountain top and a great view. It joins the Northern Wilderness, the Outcast Fortress, the Dwarven Kingdom and sealed lands (the World of Chaos, the Fire Grotto, a stone circle).
472.mood: Ravens wheeling in grey mist, wet black rock, sudden dizzy views when the mist parts.
472.creatures: Giant ravens, mountain trolls, rock wyverns, outcast scouts (15-25).
472.items: A raven-feather cloak, a troll-hide belt, an outcast's crossbow.

415.name: Quickstream
415.theme: A fast ocean current that runs out of Mira Retrum into the Southern Ocean, past Cape Voogk, and fades away to the east. You ride it in a boat; it carries you along.
415.mood: Speed, spray and the roar of moving water; then calm as it fades.
415.creatures: Flying fish and a stray shark following boats (5-12).

521.name: The Winterwood
521.theme: A snowbound pine forest beyond the Northern Wilderness, running to a glacier's end and the sealed Winterlands: paths through the trees, clusters of trees, small caves, a narrow mountain path and a rocky northern outlook.
521.mood: Hushed snow, black pine, cold stars; beautiful and dangerous.
521.creatures: Snow owls and white stags (7-11), winter wolves and a frost troll (13-17).
521.items: A white stag's antler, a frost-wolf pelt cloak, a pinewood bow.

471.name: Badlands II
471.theme: Bleak, broken country east of the Trade Road: the Black Hills, desolate plains crossed by the Old Gravel Road, the haunted Spirit Wood with a forest lodge, the Canyon of Khel-zaram, the Hill of the Hanged Man, the Bridge of Death and a sundered bridge, a rickety rope bridge over a ravine, the icy claw of Malebranche, the dark pillars, and Durgar's Gate, the doors to the Dwarven Kingdom of Aredrel. The dark castle of Ostragoth and a draconian camp lie beyond (sealed).
471.mood: Grey, wind-scoured and grim; ghosts in the Spirit Wood; vertigo on the bridges.
471.creatures: Carrion crows and badland jackals (6-10), gnolls and a hill troll on the plains (10-14), restless spirits and a hanged man's ghost in the Spirit Wood (12-16).
471.items: A gnoll's flail, a hangman's rope token, a lodge-keeper's lantern, spirit-ash.

403.name: Garathorm Wall
403.theme: The walk along the top of Garathorm's great curtain wall: a parapet of pale weathered stone with crenels and arrow slits, guard towers and stairheads at the four turns, braziers and racks of spears, banners of the city. Inward the roofs, spires and smoke of the Inner City, the Temple dome and the market; outward the plains, the Trade Road and the far hills. Gulls and crows ride the wind. The watch walks it day and night.
403.mood: High, windy and watchful; the city at your back, the wide world in front.

431.name: Garathorm Cathedral
431.theme: Garathorm's old cathedral, abandoned when its bishop turned to darker prayers, standing beyond the walls in a shaded churchyard of leaning graves and a mausoleum. Inside: the great hall of fallen pews under a broken rose window, galleries, a huge silent organ, the sacristy, a stair up the tower to the belfry and the roof. Secret passages behind the panelling lead down to catacombs, bone tunnels lined with skulls, vaults and a well shaft, and at the heart a diamond altar where the Hollow Bishop keeps his vigil. The dead do not rest here.
431.mood: Holy ground gone wrong: dust, cold candle-wax, dead silence broken by a far bell.

517.name: Garathorm School House
517.theme: The city's school house on a dirt track: a two-storey timber and stone building with hallways of pegs and slates, classrooms for philosophy, mathematics, history and science, a woodcrafting workshop, a fencing hall, the principal's, counselor's, coach's and janitor's offices, a stable behind and an outhouse. Lessons, chalk, ink and noise; a safe and gentle place for the young.
517.mood: Warm, busy and a little comic: chalk dust, scuffed floors, a bell for lessons.

420.name: Fameland
420.theme: A hall of heroes reached from Garathorm: the Gate of Fameland, the Way of Heroes, the Halls of Eternity and of Victory, the Chambers of Heroes, the Chambers of Sorrow, the Chamber of the Fallen Ones, the Rooms of Mercy and of Honour, and the Corridors of Remembrance. Marble statues, honour rolls carved in stone, trophies and banners of old wars, braziers that never go out. The spirits of the honoured dead still walk here and test the living.
420.mood: Solemn, grand and haunted by honour; marble, gold leaf and eternal flame.

418.name: Garathorm Vineyard
418.theme: The vintner's house above Garathorm's vineyard: a modest bedroom, a stair down to a vaulted wine cellar of casks, and a storage room of racked bottles, cobwebbed and dark, where something large has spun its web.
418.mood: Cool, musty and sweet with old wine.

481.name: Ghenna
481.theme: Ghenna, the city of evil: a walled town of crooked streets, hedge mazes and a fountain of tears, where the smell of decay never lifts. Barrow mounds lie outside its limits; inside are taverns and dens, a covered walkway, a golem-guarded hall, the Swordmaster's arena, an efreeti's chamber, and under it all slimy footpaths, caves and long sloping tunnels down to the lair of a deep dragon and a deepspawn. Missionaries come here to save souls; few leave.
481.mood: Rotten, menacing and decadent: decay, hedges that twist back on themselves, things watching from doorways.

475.name: World Of Chaos
475.theme: A realm a mad builder dreamed into being, reached from Mount Ravenmist past a lonely cabin: a Path of Bones paved with skulls and femurs winding through broken ground, huge black pillars that hum, a walled building of impossible proportions (a front hall, a hall of pillars, a dimly lit library, a room filled with mirrors, a mind-boggling winding staircase, a deformed gate), and a Lake of Blood with rocky shores and a small island in its middle where a way leads down to the evil city of Ghenna. Nothing here is quite the right shape.
475.mood: Unsettling and wrong: red water, bone underfoot, angles that do not add up, a silence that waits.

9.name: Minos River Island
9.theme: A small island in the river where King Minos the Minotaur keeps his court in a sunken pit: a nameless landing place, then the Pit of Minos, a sunken arena of rough stone ringed with bones and broken weapons, its passages worn by the hooves of the bull-king and his warband (General Woundwort, a gruff warrior rabbit, and the henchmen Franz and Hanz). River creatures (a sea hag, a merman, crabs, a dragon turtle) haunt the island's edges.
9.mood: Hot, dusty and brutal: the smell of beast and old blood, the river always rushing somewhere near.

423.name: Hommlet
423.theme: The upper floors and hidden store rooms above the farm village of Hommlet on the Trade Road: the private rooms over the inn where three strangers lodge (Gundigoot, Zert and Furnok, agents of a hidden cult), store rooms with false walls, a secret store room, an upper hall, and over the village church the Sacred Trophies Gallery, the assistant cleric's quarters and the chief priest's chambers, where the cult's real master hides in plain sight.
423.mood: Homely on the surface (timber, whitewash, the smell of bread and ale from below), sinister beneath: locked chests, hidden symbols, an eye carved where no one looks.

482.name: Haunted House
482.theme: A great old house beyond the cathedral fields, abandoned when its family died one by one and never truly left: a gate and a front yard gone to weeds, a grand foyer, a library, a sitting room, a living room, a greenhouse of dead plants, a kitchen, a servants' corridor, the chef's and cook's rooms, water closets, collapsed rooms, bedrooms and an attic. A gate on its far side opens on an abandoned carnival.
482.mood: Dusty, creaking and wrong: portraits whose eyes follow, cold spots, a piano that plays itself, footsteps upstairs when no one is there.

479.name: Ancalador
479.theme: Ancalador, a dragon of stone so vast that a whole realm lies inside it: from a wild valley you climb into its open mouth, past stone tonsils and down its throat to the lungs and the heart, into a stomach where an acid forest grows and wooden bridges cross the digesting dark, through the pancreas and the coiling small and large intestines to the tail. Hidden within lies the Necromancers' Guild of the Bloodstone: an undead garden, a macabre amphitheatre, the Temple of Death, cold storage, a kennel of the dead, an operating room, the guildhall and the Altar of Annihilation.
479.mood: Organic and strange: ribbed stone walls that seem to breathe, acid hiss, a slow heartbeat underfoot; then grave-cold and candle-black in the guild.
